claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist in an as-produced single-phase solid-solution state.
Ti produces moderate lattice distortion in single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The lattice distortion in single-phase equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is insufficient to impede dislocation motion significantly.
The absence of nanoscale secondary precipitates allows the starting alloy to retain high plasticity.
The absence of nanoscale secondary precipitates contributes to good machinability in the starting alloy.
The absence of nanoscale secondary precipitates is responsible for the relatively low hardness and strength of the starting alloy.
Sigma, R, and Laves phases are possible phases in the CoCrFeNiTix alloy system.
Changing Ti concentration can transform CoCrFeNiTix from a simple FCC structure to sigma, R, or Laves-containing structures.
Controlled annealing at unchanged equimolar composition can nucleate fine sigma, R, or Laves precipitates without gross phase segregation.
Fine secondary precipitates formed by post-treatment act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Precipitate pinning impedes dislocation glide more effectively than the uniform moderate lattice distortion of the single-phase alloy.
Post-treatments such as aging, annealing, and thermomechanical processing can enhance the mechanical performance of high-entropy alloys.
Annealing-induced fine precipitates will increase the hardness of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi relative to the untreated single-phase alloy.
Annealing-induced fine precipitates will increase the tensile or compressive strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi relative to the untreated alloy.
The increase in hardness and strength caused by precipitation will be accompanied by reduced ductility.
The proposed relationships are limited to equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi without large-scale phase segregation, from room temperature to approximately 600 °C under quasi-static loading.
A statistically significant increase in hardness and strength must coincide with confirmed fine-precipitate formation for the proposed mechanism to pass the controlled comparison.
